simple: Post-processing effects are filters applied to the whole picture on screen, like filters on a photo app. They can make bright things glow, blur the world, change colors and mood, or add sun rays. Put them in `Lighting` and every player sees them. Put them in the player's `Camera` and only that one player sees them, which is great for things like a red screen when health is low.
analogy: Post-processing is like putting colored glass or a soft-focus lens in front of a camera. The scene itself does not change; only how it looks through the lens does.
keyPoints: Effects inside `Lighting` show for all players. Effects inside the `Camera` show only for one player.
To add one in Studio: hover over Lighting or Camera in the Explorer, click the plus button, and pick an effect.
If an effect does not appear, raise Editor Quality Level in Studio Settings, under Rendering.
`BlurEffect` blurs the whole 3D view, like when a menu is open. `DepthOfFieldEffect` blurs only things out of focus.
`ColorCorrectionEffect` changes `Brightness`, `Contrast`, `Saturation`, and `TintColor`, for example tinting the screen red at low health.
`SunRaysEffect` adds rays of light around the sun that move with the time of day.
`ColorGradingEffect` with `TonemapperPreset` set to `Retro` gives a pre-2019 Roblox look; `Default` gives vivid, high-contrast colors.

terms.post-processing: Changing the final picture after the 3D scene is drawn, like editing a photo after you take it.
terms.filter: An effect laid over the whole screen that changes how everything looks.
terms.Camera: The object that decides what each player sees. Each player has their own camera.
terms.bloom: A glow around bright lights, like squinting at a lamp.
terms.Gaussian blur: A smooth, even blur over the whole view.
terms.depth of field: Keeping one distance sharp while closer or farther things are blurry, like a phone's portrait mode.
terms.contrast: How different darks and lights are. High contrast makes darks darker and brights brighter.
terms.saturation: How strong colors are. 0 change is normal; lower looks washed out; higher looks extra colorful.
terms.tint: A color laid over the screen. A red tint makes everything look reddish.
terms.tone mapper: The step that turns the game's light values into colors your screen can show.
terms.rendering quality: How detailed the graphics are. Some effects only show at higher quality.

example.title: Red screen when health is low
example.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local camera = Workspace.CurrentCamera

-- This effect is in the Camera, so only this player sees it
local lowHealthTint = Instance.new("ColorCorrectionEffect")
lowHealthTint.TintColor = Color3.fromRGB(255, 120, 120)
lowHealthTint.Saturation = -0.3
lowHealthTint.Enabled = false
lowHealthTint.Parent = camera

local function onCharacterAdded(character)
	local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
	lowHealthTint.Enabled = false
	humanoid.HealthChanged:Connect(function(health)
		-- Turn the tint on below 30 percent health
		lowHealthTint.Enabled = health < humanoid.MaxHealth * 0.3
	end)
end

if player.Character then
	onCharacterAdded(player.Character)
end
player.CharacterAdded:Connect(onCharacterAdded)
explain: The LocalScript creates a `ColorCorrectionEffect` and puts it in this player's camera.
`TintColor` makes the screen reddish and the negative `Saturation` makes colors a bit duller.
It starts turned off with `Enabled = false`.
Whenever health changes, the tint turns on if health is under 30 percent of max health, and off otherwise.
It reconnects each time the character respawns.

watchOut: Putting a personal effect like a menu blur in Lighting. Everyone would see it; use the player's Camera.
Thinking an effect is broken in Studio. Check that Editor Quality Level is set high.
Overdoing bloom or blur. Too much makes the game hard to see; use small values.
